motivation: The shipped five-session plan stops when an intraday wick crosses the Potter cost-basis midpoint, even though the source-derived doctrine explicitly gives candle closes priority over wick extremes. The 2026-08-13 horizon sweep left stop placement as the only untested part of exit geometry, and the 2026-08-18 retest-entry rule was falsified.
hypothesis: For source-valid bullish Potter breaks, requiring a completed daily close beyond cost basis before invalidation removes recoverable wick stop-outs and produces positive net five-session expectancy that beats both the shipped wick-stop plan on the exact same setups and same-day arbitrary exposure.
null: Close-based invalidation is not positive after 25 bps per side, does not improve the exact same setups with dependence-aware significance, or does not beat same-day same-universe drift.

design.entry_set: Records with feature_version=4 and potter_passed=1. Signals are fixed from the pinned index; detection is not re-run.
design.independence: Within each ticker and direction, keep the earliest signal then embargo the next five sessions so outcome windows do not overlap. Statistics additionally aggregate by entry day and use Newey-West lag 5.
design.risk_denominator: The exact shipped risk_pct_used, whose price level is the Potter cost-basis midpoint. No stop-distance tuning is allowed.
design.control: Production walk_triple_barrier: intraday Low/High crossing cost basis exits at the stop (or worse opening gap), no profit target, five future daily bars.
design.treatment: The same cost-basis price invalidates only when a completed future daily Close is beyond it. Exit at that Close, allowing losses beyond -1R; otherwise exit at the fifth-bar Close. No target and no intraday recovery assumption.
design.costs: Subtract 25 bps per side (0.50 percentage points round trip) from each return before dividing by the unchanged risk denominator.
design.drift_placebo: On the treatment cohort's entry days, evaluate the identical close-invalidation plan across every cached ticker with that ticker/direction's median treatment-cohort risk. Compare day means on shared days.

controls.input_hashes: Abort unless both pinned hashes match.
controls.baseline_reproduction: Before treatment results are read, the production barrier re-walk on cached bars must match stored index gross R in aggregate: absolute delta mean <= 0.005 R and Pearson correlation >= 0.99. This permits vendor revision noise but not a broken harness.
controls.fixed_cohort: Treatment and production control use exactly the same non-overlapping rows and five complete future bars.
controls.adverse_fill: A close-based stop fills at the observed invalidating Close, not at the cost-basis line, so delayed invalidation can lose more than 1R.
controls.dependence: All headline t-statistics use entry-day means and Newey-West lag 5.

acceptance_gates.coverage: At least 100 bullish rows and 40 independent entry days.
acceptance_gates.absolute: Bullish treatment day-mean net R > 0 and HAC t >= 2.0.
acceptance_gates.same_setup: Paired treatment-minus-production day-mean margin > 0 and HAC t >= 2.0.
acceptance_gates.drift: Treatment-minus-placebo day-mean margin > 0 and HAC t >= 2.0.
acceptance_gates.decision: All four gates must pass. A pass authorizes only a separately versioned shadow/walk-forward confirmation; this experiment cannot change production, promotion, paper trading, or live readiness by itself. Any failed gate closes this exact daily-close/cost-basis rule with no direction, threshold, delay, or stop-distance rescue.

known_limitations: The immutable bar cache ends before the newest index rows; rows without five complete cached future sessions are excluded before either arm is evaluated.
A daily close stop is modeled at the closing price and charged the production cost floor; real market-on-close slippage could be worse.
The experiment does not test intraday or multi-timeframe invalidation, a different cost-basis level, ATR buffers, or profit targets.
